::: {.project-deck}
Project Myogenesis investigates how microgravity influences human skeletal muscle stem-cell function
and the capacity to maintain and regenerate muscle.
:::

## A human muscle experiment in orbit

Human skeletal muscle stem cells were cultured aboard the International Space Station during
Axiom Mission 4 in a BioServe Space Technologies flight habitat, with matched ground controls at
inStem.

The experiment pairs on-orbit imaging with post-flight molecular and metabolic measurements.
Analysis is underway; results and intervention details will be shared only after disclosure and
publication clearance.

## Microgravity as an experimental context

Spaceflight produces rapid physiological deconditioning and creates a distinctive setting in which
to investigate muscle maintenance and repair. Comparing flight samples with matched ground controls
can reveal cellular responses that are difficult to isolate in conventional models while informing
questions relevant to both human spaceflight and disuse on Earth.

## Partners

The project brings together ISRO, Axiom Space, BioServe Space Technologies and Siobhan Malany at the
University of Florida.

## Mission coverage

Nature India reported on Project Myogenesis as part of its coverage of the Indian experiments selected
for Axiom Mission 4. Axiom Space also documented the project and its operation aboard the ISS.
